{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Outsourcing Agreement (MSL / IBM)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Outsourcing Agreement — verified findings  

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. Overall the risk allocation is favourable to us: vendor-side indemnity, IP ownership, warranty, exit/transition, audit rights and MFN pricing all run in our direction, and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum purchase commitment or liquidated damages burden on us. Licence grants run from us to MSL only, which is stronger than the preferred inbound licence position and should not be broadened.

Four verified deviations and one gap require attention:

- **Limitation of liability (critical).** The mutual cap is set at 3% of bill-of-materials value across the whole term — below six months' fees, which is walk-away territory — and there are no carve-outs, so MSL's indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside the cap. This is our priority ask.
- **Assignment (high).** Consent is required with no reasonableness standard and no affiliate/successor carve-out for us, and MSL may terminate on a change of control of our business.
- **Non-solicitation (medium).** One-way restriction on us, covering all Transferred Employees, running years from the Effective Date.
- **Auto-renewal (low).** Non-renewal notice windows of six and twelve months, well beyond the 90-day walk-away line.
- **Vendor insurance (low).** No programme-level insurance covenant despite MSL holding our inventory and tooling and accessing our systems and customer data.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 15.3 Limitations of Liability | Cap basis (3% of BOM value across the term) sits below six months' fees and there are no carve-outs. Redline: greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable or USD 1,000,000, plus one carve-out sentence. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 15.1 Scope of MSL's Indemnity | Full vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP, non-compliance with law and failure to perform warranty/support; carve-outs limited to our own inputs. No data-breach or gross negligence prong — noted only. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 13.0 Intellectual and Industrial Property | MSL assigns all IP in Products and related inventions to us; no rights in our pre-existing IP pass to MSL; no joint ownership. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 16.2 Assignment | No reasonableness standard or affiliate/successor carve-out for us; § 5.1(b)(v) lets MSL terminate on our change of control. Redline: reasonableness standard, our affiliate/successor carve-out, bar on MSL assigning to a competitor, and narrow the § 5.1(b)(v) trigger to MSL. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 6.0 Purchase of Products | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us; purchasing is order-driven and orders are cancellable. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 6.1 Cancellation of Purchase Order | No LDs, penalties or early-termination fees on us; the only penalty mechanic runs against MSL. Termination amounts are cost recovery, not stipulated damages. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.0 Intellectual and Industrial Property | All grants run from us to MSL and are appropriately restrictive; we hold ownership rather than a licence. Should not be broadened. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 9.0 Personnel | No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction on us; § 9.0(e) expressly contemplates migration to a competitive supplier. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 7.0 Audit | All audit and inspection rights run in our favour; MSL has no reciprocal right. § 16.14 imposes only mutual five-year record retention. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 16.9 Governing Law | New York law, New York courts, no arbitration. Non-exclusive wording and mutual jury-trial waiver/limitations period noted only. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | Attachment 1 | The only MFN language runs in our favour (most favoured customer engineering pricing). No matching obligation on us. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Compliant** | § 6.0 Purchase of Products | No minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume cap; orders cancellable at any time. Forecast-accuracy true-up and default-scenario Parts buyback noted, not flagged. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 9.0 Personnel | One-way, covers all Transferred Employees, runs years from the Effective Date. Redline: mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from end of involvement, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | Compliant | § 5.2 Rights Upon Termination | Uncapped transition assistance to us or our designee, plus return of documentation and confidential media; § 13.2 c) allows return on demand. Redacted return period and absence of a machine-readable format spec noted only. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 Scope of Warranty | Express conformance, quality and workmanship warranty with stated periods, latent-defect coverage, repair/replace/refund remedies and recall costs. "In lieu of" wording disclaims only implied terms. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 16.21 Excused Exceptions to MSL Performance | No programme-level insurance covenant; only asset-specific cover. Insert new § 16.22 requiring CGL, E&O, workers' compensation and cyber coverage with certificates. |
| Low | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 4.0 Term | Six-month (Base) and twelve-month (Attachment § 2.0) non-renewal windows exceed the 90-day walk-away line. Redline: 30-day opt-out for us, 12-month renewals, 60-day reminder, renewal uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. MSL's notice period left intact for supply continuity. |

**Not relied upon pending verification:** a proposed termination-for-convenience finding (rule T4C, § 4.0 Term) did not pass verification. We are re-checking the termination provisions before raising any convenience-exit position with MSL.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Liability cap basis (§ 15.3 b)).** A cap measured as 3% of bill-of-materials value over the term sits below six months' fees and is walk-away under the playbook. We need the 12-months'-fees / USD 1,000,000 floor and carve-outs for MSL's § 15.1 indemnity, confidentiality (§ 13.2 and the AECI), gross negligence and willful misconduct.
2. **Assignment consent (§ 16.2) with MSL's change-of-control termination right (§ 5.1(b)(v)).** Absence of any affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out for us, combined with MSL's ability to terminate on a change of control of our business, is walk-away territory.
3. **Non-renewal notice windows (§ 4.0; Attachment § 2.0).** Windows longer than 90 days are walk-away; six and twelve months are materially outside tolerance.
4. **Non-solicitation duration (§ 9.0(f)).** The redacted period may sit at or beyond the 24-month walk-away line; we must see the number before agreeing anything.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. Issue the four redlines (§ 15.3, § 16.2 with § 5.1(b)(v), § 9.0(f), § 4.0 / Attachment § 2.0) and the new § 16.22 insurance insert, each with a short [Playbook] comment stating the position and, where sensible, the fallback.
2. Ask MSL to unredact the non-solicit period (§ 9.0(f)), the warranty durations (§ 19), the post-termination return period (§ 5.2 a) iii; Attachment 6 § 3(a)) and the contractual limitations period (§ 16.9) so we can confirm compliance.
3. Request MSL's current certificates of insurance to size the § 16.22 limits; fall back to E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M if the preferred limits are resisted.
4. Complete verification of the termination-for-convenience analysis before tabling any § 5 exit right.
5. Hold the line on the favourable provisions: do not trade away the § 15.1 indemnity scope, § 13.1/13.2 ownership and assignment, § 7.0 audit rights, the Attachment 1 most-favoured-customer pricing, or the order-driven purchasing model in § 6.0 / § 6.1. If MSL later seeks a reciprocal audit right, hold it to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, off-site, at MSL's cost absent a 5% underpayment, with no access to our systems.
"}
